Technical Analysis: Studio Network Solutions Announces Eon Series NAS for Scalable Video Production Workflows

Studio Network Solutions has announced the Eon Series NAS, a high-performance storage solution designed for video production workflows. The Eon Series NAS is built on a modular architecture, allowing for easy scalability and integration with existing infrastructure. By leveraging Object Storage (S3) compatibility and Microservices-based design, the Eon Series NAS aims to simplify workflow automation and reduce total cost of ownership for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers.

Operational ROI

The Eon Series NAS is expected to save money and time for broadcast CTOs by reducing operational overhead in the ingest and transcoding workflow steps. With its high-performance storage and automated workflow capabilities, the Eon Series NAS can accelerate content delivery by up to 30% and lower infrastructure costs by up to 25%. Additionally, the Eon Series NAS eliminates manual QC effort by integrating with existing Media Asset Management (MAM) systems, allowing for automated quality control and validation of ingested content.

In comparison to existing approaches, the Eon Series NAS offers a more scalable and flexible solution for video production workflows. Traditional NAS solutions often require manual intervention and are limited in their ability to scale, resulting in increased operational overhead and reduced efficiency. The Eon Series NAS, on the other hand, provides a modular and automated solution that can easily integrate with existing infrastructure, reducing the need for manual intervention and increasing overall workflow efficiency.

Security & Integration

The Eon Series NAS is designed to fit seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with support for Kubernetes and API Orchestration. The solution also provides robust security features, including encryption and access controls, to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of stored content. In terms of compliance, the Eon Series NAS meets relevant standards and requirements, including those related to Egress Costs and data protection. For ingest and playout integration, the Eon Series NAS supports ST 2110 and NMOS protocols, allowing for easy integration with existing IP-based infrastructure.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The Eon Series NAS requires a minimum of 10GbE network connectivity and a compatible S3 API to ensure optimal performance and integration with existing infrastructure.
  • Compatibility: The Eon Series NAS is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04 protocols, ensuring seamless integration with existing IP-based infrastructure and ingest/playout systems.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the development of new Object Storage (S3) standards and protocols, such as the upcoming S3 API version 2.0, to ensure continued compatibility and optimal performance of the Eon Series NAS.

The announcement of the Eon Series NAS signals a significant shift towards more scalable and automated video production workflows, and engineering teams should prioritize evaluating and integrating this solution into their existing infrastructure to take advantage of its operational and cost benefits. By doing so, broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers can improve the efficiency and reliability of their workflows, while also reducing costs and improving overall ROI.

Analysis: ST 2110 support in NAS devices enables efficient video production workflows by facilitating IP-based transport of uncompressed video and audio signals, reducing latency and increasing bitrate capacity.
